title: FULL OUTER JOIN
description: A FULL OUTER JOIN keeps every row from BOTH tables, matched where possible and padded with NULLs on whichever side has no match. Write a query that returns every department's `name` alongside every employee's `first_name`, joined on department - so a department with no employees AND an employee with no department both still appear.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: FULL OUTER JOIN

FULL OUTER JOIN is a LEFT JOIN and a RIGHT JOIN at once: a department with no employees gets a NULL employee name, and an employee with no department gets a NULL department name - neither side ever gets silently dropped.
Select departments.name and employees.first_name, using departments FULL OUTER JOIN employees ON departments.id = employees.department_id.
expected_behavior: Returns every matched pair, plus a NULL-employee row for any empty department and a NULL-department row for any employee with no department.
solution: SELECT departments.name, employees.first_name FROM departments FULL OUTER JOIN employees ON departments.id = employees.department_id;
explanation: FULL OUTER JOIN is the least common of the four, but it's exactly what you reach for when you need to see BOTH sides' orphans in one result - unmatched departments and unmatched employees together.
